findings.description: The instance user data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data can be retrieved by principals with instance or metadata access and is commonly exposed through state, logs, and host compromise, allowing abuse of the associated IAM principal.
Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's SSH service to arbitrary internet hosts and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
The EBS volume does not enable encryption, so data written to this attached disk may be stored unencrypted at rest unless account-level default encryption is relied upon outside this configuration.
The snapshot is created from an EBS volume that is not configured for encryption, so the backup can contain the volume's data without encryption at rest.
The bucket has no server-side encryption configuration. VPC flow logs archived here may therefore be stored without bucket-level encryption at rest.
